name: Baseline: no reform beyond current law
assumptions: Current law, including the 2025 budget law (P.L. 119-21) and P.L. 119-75, runs as written; The Senate keeps the legislative filibuster; Recent trends in executive action and court rulings continue
dq_why: Mid-decade redraws and the narrower Section 2 standard after Louisiana v. Callais raise C4: Officeholders' control over election rules. The Federal Election Commission stays without a quorum.
ge_why: Workforce losses, funding lapses and closed digital service teams weigh on D5: Quality of public services.
ep_why: Productivity grows near its recent trend; tariffs add costs.
eq_why: Stock prices push the top 1% share to records, and the 2025 law shifts resources toward higher-income households.

name: State and local track by 2030
assumptions: Initiatives and statutes pass in some states: nomination rules, local elections moved onto the statewide calendar, housing allowed by right, wage floors and child credits; No federal rules change; Federal administrative capacity is restored only if the administration that takes office in 2029 chooses to restore it
dq_why: C2: How often the primary decides the winner falls where nomination rules change, and local turnout rises when local elections share the ballot with statewide contests.
ge_why: State capacity rises where it is funded; federal capacity follows the administration.
ep: slightly up in metro areas that reform housing rules
ep_why: New housing supply takes three to ten years to arrive.
eq: up for renters and low-income families in reform states
eq_why: Wage floors, credits and housing supply help; top shares barely move.

name: A coherent federal package
assumptions: A Senate majority changes the filibuster and uses the change first on rules for elections and government; Statutes pass on the civil service, inspectors general, emergency powers, tariffs and public research; A permanent refundable child credit passes through budget reconciliation
dq: up on structure; uncertain on behavior
dq_why: Maps, the visibility of political money and the schedule of court appointments change; evidence that any of it lowers affective polarization is weak.
ge_why: Capacity measures have the best-identified evidence and work through administration in two to five years.
ep_why: Public research pays off over decades; competition measures act one sector at a time.
eq: up quickly on income; slowly on wealth
eq_why: Transfers act in the year they pay, as in 2021; taxes on capital act over decades.

name: Parties first: fusion voting and public funding for parties
assumptions: R-47: Allow fusion voting and consider public support for parties, and R-07: Match small donations or give voters campaign vouchers, adopted widely
dq_why: Coalitions can form without one candidate splitting the vote of another (the spoiler problem).
ge: same as scenario ii (state and local track)
ep: same as scenario ii (state and local track)
eq: same as scenario ii (state and local track)

name: Capacity first: civil service, IRS, inspectors general, congressional staff and digital service
assumptions: R-17: Protect a professional career civil service; R-27: Rebuild skilled enforcement of taxes already owed; R-15: Give watchdogs usable remedies when oversight is obstructed; R-13: Rebuild Congress's own expertise; R-39: Build public teams that can deliver digital services
ge_why: A change made by statute lasts; one made by executive order can be undone by the next order.
ep: same as scenario ii (state and local track)
eq_why: More revenue is collected, and existing benefits reach more of the people eligible for them.

name: Competition and labor first
assumptions: R-19: Address drug-middleman conflicts and sector-specific market power; R-20: Enforce merger rules in markets for goods and labor; R-21: Make labor-law remedies timely and help secure first contracts; R-22: Set industry-wide standards through bargaining or wage boards; R-38: Limit competitors' use of shared private data to set prices; R-44: Open digital platform markets to effective competition
dq: slightly up if union membership rises
dq_why: Through Loop R15: Unions, civic ties and equal turnout reinforce each other, run in reverse: stronger unions sustain organizations that bring people into civic life.
ep: prices down in affected sectors; employment effects mixed

name: Constitutional amendments
assumptions: R-50: Assess constitutional representation changes and the popular-vote compact, and R-16: Regular Supreme Court appointments and enforceable ethics, adopted by constitutional amendment under Article V
dq_why: Supermajorities of the size Article V requires are unlikely to form by 2036.

name: Forbearance: restraint by officials without new rules
assumptions: Officials restrain themselves without new rules
dq: flat, or down if one side stops holding back
dq_why: Unwritten norms bind only while both sides keep them.
